To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a region of perinventricular heterotopia in an epilepsy patient was characterized by a cortical-like spectroscopic composition and was interconnected by fiber pathways with nearby cortical fundi, which was demonstrated by functional and resting-state connectivity MRI.

the heterotopic region demonstrated cortical-like composition, connectivity with nearby cortical fundi, functional modulation while the patient watched video scenes of biological movement, and directionality within an inter-connected network during a resting-state task.
we have shown that the heterotopic tissue in a single patient was functionally connected to the patient's normal cortical tissue and was functionally active while the patient was watching a cartoon.

the authors' results suggest that a heterotopionic region of the human brain may be functionally connected with nearby cortical fundi and may be involved in the perception and/or production of biological motion, and that this region may have a unique role in cognition, as suggested by its rsfMRI connectivity pattern.

PVNHs, which have been traditionally viewed as a developmental anomaly, may in fact be a neuroanatomical substrate for the emergence of a distinct form of cortical architecture that is functionally interconnected to other cortical and cerebellum regions, and may be associated with the emergence of unique forms of cognition and behavior.
